model_output_raw.confidence_explanation: The evidence shows a clear pattern of an authorized user (user_04) with 'read_only' access and a baseline of 0 downloads per day performing 6 file downloads. Crucially, this user accessed files outside their department (Engineering projects) and worked significantly outside their normal hours (until 19:00, 2 hours past their 17:00 limit). This behavior deviates sharply from their baseline and role constraints, indicating unauthorized data exfiltration.

attack_chain.description: user_04 logs in from normal IP within normal hours.
user_04 performs first file download (accounts_receivable), violating baseline of 0 downloads/day.
user_04 performs second download (accounts_payable), establishing a pattern of bulk data collection.
user_04 accesses cross-department data (Engineering project_alpha), violating departmental scope.
user_04 downloads sensitive tax data (tax_withholdings), escalating data sensitivity.
user_04 accesses second cross-department directory (Engineering project_beta).
user_04 downloads bank reconciliation data, furthering financial data exfiltration.
user_04 downloads general ledger (5MB), a large sensitive financial file.
user_04 accesses cross-department data again at 17:15, outside normal working hours (09:00-17:00).
user_04 logs out at 19:00, having worked 2 hours past their authorized shift end.

gaps: No metadata (ticket numbers or manager approval) explaining the cross-department access or off-hours work.
No evidence of user_04's specific job duties requiring access to Engineering project files.
No network egress logs to confirm if the downloaded files were successfully exfiltrated to an external location.
model_output_raw.narrative: user_04, a junior accountant with read-only access and a baseline of zero daily downloads, engaged in a systematic data exfiltration campaign. The user downloaded six sensitive financial files and accessed engineering project data outside their department, continuing these activities two hours past their authorized shift end time. This pattern of behavior strongly indicates an insider threat attempting to steal financial and project data.
